reader.title: Lynching of Manuel Bowers
bases: Bowers, accused of a killing and captured by a posse, was hanged to a tree in his own yard a few days later, with no court, trial or officer mentioned (A1).

Bowers was hanged to a tree in his yard days after a posse captured him for the killing of Huguely, which points to an extralegal killing in reprisal for the alleged crime (A1); the brief does not say who hanged him or how many took part, so the group element rests only on the posse's earlier role.
The only report found is one sentence in the St. Landry Democrat's state-news column (A1).

summary.text: The lynching of Manuel Bowers was the hanging of a Black man to a tree in his own yard in Louisiana in May 1888, a few days after a posse captured him near Coushatta.
Bowers was accused of shooting and killing Chas. Huguely near Indian Village about two weeks earlier.
The only account found is a single sentence in a weekly paper's column of state news, which named no one in the hanging party.
According to the St. Landry Democrat of May 26, 1888, Chas. Huguely was shot and killed near Indian Village roughly a fortnight before that issue.
The paper attributed the killing to Bowers, whom it described as "colored," and stated his guilt as fact rather than as a charge.
It gave no motive for the shooting, no circumstances, and no race for Huguely.
A posse later captured Bowers near Coushatta, "a few days" before the report appeared.
He was then "hanged to a tree in his own yard," in the paper's words.
The item, written in the passive voice, did not say whether the posse itself carried out the hanging, how many people took part, or whether any officer was present.
No report of an inquest, arrest or official response appears in the coverage.
The St. Landry Democrat ran the news as one line in its "Louisiana News" column, placed between a report of a merchant stabbed at Robeline and a crop note from Cottonport.
The item carried no headline of its own and no comment on the hanging, and it treated the accusation against Bowers as settled.
No other newspaper account of the hanging, and no follow-up report, was found.

accounts.label: State-news brief
accounts.gist: Bowers, who 'shot and killed' Huguely, was captured by a posse near Coushatta and then hanged to a tree in his own yard; no hanging party is named.

framing.detail: The St. Landry Democrat ran the hanging as one line in its 'Louisiana News' column between a stabbing and a crop report, treating Bowers's guilt as fact and the hanging without comment.

record_check.dossier: Garbled wording; the paper says Bowers 'shot and killed' Huguely, stated as fact, and it remains an accusation: accused of shooting and killing Chas. Huguely near Indian Village.
A posse captured Bowers; the brief does not say who hanged him.
Capture by a posse and hanging to a tree; 'hanging' is the act of killing.
Two deaths only if the earlier killing of Huguely is counted; the lynching itself killed one person (Bowers). Huguely's race is not given.
Bowers had been captured by a posse a few days before he was hanged; who held him is not stated.
Places named: Indian Village (killing of Huguely), near Coushatta (capture), his own yard (hanging); no parish is given.
